insights.summary: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue was ₹602 Cr (up 18.5%) with EBITDA of ₹131 Cr (21.8%) and PAT of ₹73 Cr; standalone revenue rose 31% with a 28% margin. A record 1,911 machines were dispatched and the order book is ₹5,082 Cr. The MD kept FY27 guidance (25-30% growth, 25% margin, 8,000+ machines, Huron about ₹300 Cr) and said H2 should be about 60% of the year as the new plant, foundry and Huron dispatches come in.

what_changed.text: 25-30% revenue growth, 25% margin, 8,000+ machines for FY27
ECMS capital subsidy approval of about ₹255 Cr on ₹1,020 Cr of electronics investment
Order intake of ₹800 Cr in Q2 took the order book to ₹5,082 Cr; H1 intake is already above the ₹2,500-3,000 Cr full-year guide
Huron machine dispatches only from Q3-Q4 as export licences arrive

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: we are very much confident to reach to 25% margin, what we have guided to market, and we are about to maintaining those things.

analyst_questions.answer: Intake already above guide; Q2 and Q3 are the heavy intake quarters; aerospace and defence orders delayed by tenders not opening.
Confident; H2 is better than H1 and Huron revenue of about ₹60 Cr unrecognised in H1 flows in H2.
French authorities have been silent since April; controller supply from Japan and Europe is tight but inventory was planned.

analyst_questions.topic: Can India make its own controllers?
analyst_questions.answer: 110+ engineers in controller R&D, 40-50 more to be added; hardware plant planned under the ECMS scheme.

red_flags.text: H1 consolidated margin (about 22%) is well below the 25% promise; H2 must do about 28% to deliver it.
Aerospace and defence order intake fell in Q2 as tenders were delayed; autos and general engineering rose.
French investigation into Huron is unresolved (status quo since April); export licences for Huron machines are slow.
Controller supply from Japan and Europe is stretched; lead times doubled.

watch_next: Huron revenue ramp (₹80-100 Cr in Q3 is the analyst's expectation)
Foundry start and capex near ₹450-500 Cr
Aerospace and defence order intake recovering

business_snapshot.what_they_make: CNC machine tools, from entry-level to 5-axis turn-mill, with a foundry and in-house machining
business_snapshot.customers: Automotive, aerospace and defence (21% of Q2 revenue), general engineering, electronics, railways; 15,000+ customers
business_snapshot.revenue_mix: Q2: automotive 36%, general engineering 28%, aerospace and defence 21%, electronics 7%
business_snapshot.demand_drivers: Import substitution (about 62% of Indian CNC demand is imported), EV and defence capex, ECMS electronics scheme
